title: core.audio.effect / core.audio.ambience — per-effect generation sidecar
description: Adopted VERBATIM from the splat-foley per-effect sidecar (splat-foley's sfx/<slug>.json) because that shape is already in production and re-inventing it would lose the field data. Every field below exists in real splat-foley output; werk adds only optional keys, all marked. One sidecar accompanies one effect and its WAV takes. An 'ambience' node uses this identical schema with category 'ambience'; the node type differs only so a browser can separate beds from one-shots. Law 9: this file is the generation record, the A/B audition list AND the quality gate evidence. CAREFUL: this schema and core.audio.package.schema.json use DIFFERENT NAMES FOR THE SAME VALUE, permanently, because both were adopted verbatim from a real pipeline rather than harmonised. Here the prompt is 'prompt_used'; in the package index it is effects[].prompt. Here the sample rate is audio_format.sample_rate_hz; the package index does not carry it at all. A reader that carries a field name across gets an empty string and no error. The full mapping table is in spec/SPEC.md section 3.9. This sidecar is the authority on ONE effect; the package index is the authority on the SET.

slug.description: The effect's stable id. This is what an animation event's effect_id resolves to, and what a destruction piece's audio_effect_id names. Ids, not indices (law 4).

prompt_used.description: The exact text-to-audio prompt that produced the accepted take. Kept verbatim so the take is reproducible and so a human can see why it sounds the way it does. null (werk relaxation of the donor shape) = the sound was not generated from a prompt (recorded, synthesised, edited by hand); a writer MUST NOT invent one.

seconds.description: Requested generation length, seconds. The delivered length after refinement is refined.duration.

loopable.description: True for continuous sounds (drag, roll, wind, ambience beds). A loopable take has been cross-faded; see refined.loop_crossfade_ms.

clap_score.description: CLAP audio-text similarity between the accepted take and prompt_used. Higher is a better match to the prompt. This is a MEASURED number and is exactly why the epistemic stamp on this node is 'measured' rather than 'inferred'. null (werk relaxation of the donor shape, as variations[].clap_score already allows) = NOT MEASURED: no CLAP model was run, or there is no prompt to compare with. A writer MUST write null rather than 0 or any other number for a measurement that was not made, and a version whose only would-be measurement is null is not stamped 'measured' on its account.

attempts.description: How many generations were run before one was accepted.

accepted.description: Whether the effect passed its quality gate. A rejected effect may still ship: it is honest payload, and a consumer can choose to skip anything with accepted false.

variations.description: Alternative takes kept for A/B. Each is a real WAV in the package.

file.description: File name of the variation WAV, as produced by splat-foley (e.g. '<slug>.var2.wav'). Resolved against the node's files[] in the manifest.

refined.description: What the post-generation editor did: where it cut, what it heard, and whether the refinement actually helped. When 'reason' is present the refinement was ROLLED BACK and the raw take shipped — the record of the failed attempt is kept deliberately, because a format that only records successes cannot be audited.

kept.description: What the editor kept. Observed values: 'one_shot' (a single event isolated from the generation), 'rolled_back' (refinement discarded, raw take shipped), 'loop' (a loopable region cross-faded), 'full' (nothing trimmed). Free string rather than an enum, so a newer editor can report a new strategy without invalidating old files (law 12).

cut.description: [start_s, end_s] of the region kept from the raw generation. Note the field name says 'cut' and the value is what SURVIVED the cut; this is splat-foley's spelling and is preserved verbatim.

event.description: The single dominant event, when one was isolated.

n_events_raw.description: How many onset events the detector found in the raw generation.

events.description: Every detected event in the raw generation, in time order.

heard.description: An audio-captioning model's transcript of what is audible in the take, with intervals. INFERRED text: it is a model's opinion, it is frequently wrong about intervals, and it is kept because it makes a sound library searchable by what things sound like rather than by what they were meant to be.

duration_raw.description: Length of the raw generation, seconds.

duration.description: Length of the delivered take, seconds. This is the authoritative playback length.

clap_score_refined.description: CLAP score of the refined take. When this is lower than clap_score the refinement was rolled back and 'reason' says so.

loop_crossfade_ms.description: Cross-fade length applied at the loop point, milliseconds. Present for loopable effects.

reason.description: Why the refinement was rolled back, e.g. 'refined CLAP 0.508 < raw 0.579'.

category.description: werk addition (optional): mirrors the plan's category, so an effect sidecar is readable without the package manifest (law 3).

object.description: werk addition (optional): the described object this effect belongs to.

material.description: werk addition (optional): material class the sound represents.

interaction.description: werk addition (optional): short verb phrase, e.g. 'dragged across rough concrete'.

part_id.description: werk addition (optional): joins this sound to manifest parts[].

material_id.description: werk addition (optional): joins this sound to manifest materials[].

audio_format.description: werk addition (optional but strongly recommended): the WAV parameters, declared rather than discovered by parsing. See spec/MINI-SPECS.md for the WAV container.

epistemic.description: werk addition (optional): mirrors the manifest stamp.

start.description: seconds from the start of the RAW generation

end.description: seconds from the start of the RAW generation

peak_db.description: peak level of the event, dBFS (negative)
